question: How does a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) Type 1 handle a change to an attribute value?
options: It overwrites the old value with the new value, keeping no history
It inserts a new row and expires the old one
It adds a new column to preserve the previous value
It rejects the update to protect existing data
explanation: SCD Type 1 simply overwrites the existing attribute with the new value. It is the simplest approach and retains no history of prior values.

question: What is the main disadvantage of SCD Type 1?
options: It requires far more storage than other SCD types
Historical values are lost, so past reports cannot reflect the attribute as it once was
It creates duplicate rows for every entity
It cannot be applied to text attributes
explanation: Because Type 1 overwrites values in place, all prior history is discarded. Analytical queries can no longer reconstruct what the attribute value was at an earlier point in time.

question: In which scenario is SCD Type 1 the most appropriate choice?
options: When every historical version of an attribute must be auditable
When you need to compare current versus prior attribute values side by side
When you must track the full timeline of changes for compliance
When correcting a data entry error and no history of the wrong value is needed
explanation: Type 1 fits corrections and cases where prior values have no analytical value, such as fixing a misspelled name. When the incorrect value need not be preserved, overwriting is the simplest and correct approach.

question: After an SCD Type 1 update, how are existing fact rows that reference the dimension affected?
options: They automatically reflect the new attribute value because the surrogate key is unchanged
They must all be reinserted with new surrogate keys
They lose their foreign key relationship
They are duplicated to preserve both old and new values
explanation: Since Type 1 overwrites the attribute in the same row (same surrogate key), all facts already pointing to that dimension row instantly reflect the updated value with no changes needed to the fact table.

question: Compared to SCD Type 2, what is an advantage of SCD Type 1?
options: It provides a complete audit trail of every change
It keeps the dimension smaller and simpler with no version proliferation
It enables point-in-time historical reporting
It stores both current and previous values in separate columns
explanation: Because Type 1 never adds new rows for changes, the dimension stays compact and simple to query. Type 2 preserves history but grows the table with multiple versioned rows per entity.
